Pre-read attached: proposed-topology-v2.png (simple sketch showing warm pool + burst slabs + tenant isolation lanes) and a 1-page runbook checklist (included inline below). We'll also include a link to our SOC 2 summary and KMS integration notes in the invite.

Quick runbook checklist (1 page summary):
- Ownership: primary on-call and escalation list (name + phone/email)
- Observability: per-model latency histograms (p50/p95/p99), token-level cost breakdown, eviction rates for KV cache
- Autoscale triggers: steady-state QPS vs. burst delta thresholds, cooldown windows, max slab count
- Fallbacks: model-variant fallback order, regional failover, and local token-stream buffering (to preserve tail latency)
- Maintenance windows: recommended weekly low-traffic window for slab reprovisioning and quantization profile updates
- Post-incident: RCA template + impact window + SLO credit calculation

Notes on isolation & cost delta (high level):
- Dedicated slabs (physical isolate): strongest noisy-neighbor guarantees; typical +25–40% unit cost depending on utilization but easier SRE ownership and cert boundaries.
- Logical lanes on shared pool: lower cost at steady high utilization; needs stronger throttling and priority-based preemption for predictable p99.

Attachments in invite: proposed-topology-v2.png, nimbus-capacity-questions.pdf (your answers), sample-runbook-onepager.pdf (runbook summary), and a link to SOC 2 notes.

Calendar invite will include a Google Meet link and a short Loom recording option if any attendee can't join live — we'll record and share the transcript.
